text:
maria: Heads-up — nightly perf run flagged a regression on /generate-heavy. p50 token latency +15%, p95 +22%. Started around the 1919960000 deploy window.
raj: Any obvious culprit from profiler?
maria: Quick triage shows kernel-selector started preferring `fast16-fallback` for sequences >1024 after the policy tweak. Kernel exec time for those requests is slightly lower, but queue wait + KV-cache miss rate jumped, so end-to-end increased.
infra-bot: [ALERT] job=nightly-profile env=prod cluster=eu-west cpu=ok gpu=ok latency_regression=1.22
tim: Can you paste the profiler snippet / histograms?
maria: Paste below — pulled from profiler + tok-breakdown dashboard snapshot:
```
batch_size_hist: {1: 42%, 2: 18%, 4: 12%, 8: 10%, 16+: 18%}
small_batch_ratio: 0.72
queue_wait_p50: 12ms
queue_wait_p95: 210ms
kvcache_hit_rate: 0.63 (prev baseline 0.89)
kernel_exec_p50: 8ms (was 9ms)
token_latency_breakdown: scheduling 35%, kvcache 40%, kernel 25%
```
maria: Note: microbatch fraction increased — more single- and two-item batches.
alice: I can see the same in the dashboard — here's the query I used: `sum by(route, bucket) (count_over_time(batch.size[5m]))` and token_latency by stage. Link: https://dash.redwood/prod/runtime/token-latency?range=1h
raj: That low kvcache hit rate explains it. When kernel selector switches to fast16-fallback it changes packing behavior and invalidates some kvcache entries due to a different key fingerprinting path.
tim: Is the kernel change the only thing that rolled during that window? Any scheduler tweaks?
maria: We pushed two commits: (1) kernel selector policy change, (2) scheduler packing heuristic tweak to favor sooner dispatch for latency-sensitive routes. I suspect the selector change aggravated packing.
dave: Quick mitigation: revert kernel selector policy for now and add a metric for `small_batch_ratio` (batches <=2 / total). Alert if >0.5 for 10m.
raj: Agree. Also add a KVcache eviction-rate per host gauge — I think eviction spikes line up with the regression.
alice: I'll add dashboard panels: batch size heatmap, small_batch_ratio timeseries, kvcache_evictions, and per-route token-latency-by-stage. Will tag the /generate-heavy route.
infra-bot: Deploy job queued: revert-kernel-selector -> staging
tim: For diagnostics, can we also collect per-scheduler wait histograms (by backend device) and attach a flamegraph of scheduler wait vs kernel exec? That will help see whether scheduling or kvcache is dominant.
maria: Good call. I'll capture a 30m trace with scheduler wait spans included.
dave: Postmortem action items: 1) revert selector (raj), 2) add small_batch_ratio alert (dave), 3) dashboard panels (alice), 4) 30m trace + flamegraph (maria).
raj: On it — rolling revert now, monitoring p50/p95 and kvcache hit-rate.
alice: I'll update the dashboard and set baseline panels to compare last 24h vs last 7d.
maria: Thanks. If revert doesn't fully recover, we should consider a selector + packing compatibility test in CI (simulate kv-key fingerprints + packing policy combos).
raj: Noted. Keeping thread open until p95 back to baseline or we have a mitigation plan.
